I open when it rains and keep you dry, folded up small when the sky is high. What am I?
My hands go round and round all day, I tell you time but cannot play. What am I?

Turn my pages one by one, and worlds appear till you are done. What am I?
Small and metal, I fit a hole, unlocking doors is my whole role. What am I?
Step by step you climb on me, to reach the heights you wish to see. What am I?
Fill me with air and I will grow, prick me once and off I go. What am I?
On windy days I love to fly, a string keeps me from the sky. What am I?
I show you cities, roads, and seas, yet I fold up with the greatest ease. What am I?
Rest your head on me at night, and I'll hold your dreams till morning light. What am I?
I stretch across the river wide, so you can walk from side to side. What am I?
In the dark I glow so bright, a little flame gives you sight. What am I?
I always point you to the north, to guide your travels back and forth. What am I?
Sand runs through me grain by grain, when I'm empty, turn me again. What am I?
Look through me toward the night, and distant stars come into sight. What am I?
Heavy and iron, I sink below, to keep the ship from drifting slow. What am I?
Blow through me and I will sing, a sharp clear note is what I bring. What am I?
Beat on me and I will boom, filling up the empty room. What am I?
Give me a swing and I will chime, ringing out to mark the time. What am I?
Full of holes yet I still catch, whatever swims into my patch. What am I?
I stand in fields both night and day, to keep the hungry crows away. What am I?
My arms turn round in country breeze, grinding grain with graceful ease. What am I?
Water leaps from me up high, then falls back down and never dry. What am I?
Speak to me and I will send, your voice across to a distant friend. What am I?
Two sharp blades that cross and part, I cut the paper for your art. What am I?
I pull the iron toward my side, a hidden force I cannot hide. What am I?
Round and round forever I spin, to make the journey we begin. What am I?
I come in colors bold and bright, I fill your pages with delight. What am I?
Pack me full and off we go, to places near or far, you know. What am I?
I rise and fall to show the heat, telling if you're feverish or sweet. What am I?
Turn the key or spin the dial, I guard your secrets all the while. What am I?
Draw the bow across my strings, and sweet and sorrowed music sings. What am I?
Black and white in tidy rows, where kings and queens and knights oppose. What am I?
I pound the nail with one hard smack, to build the house or fix the shack. What am I?
With bristles wide I sweep the floor, and chase the dust right out the door. What am I?
Fill me up and heat me high, and steam will whistle from me by-and-by. What am I?
High above the town I stand, my chiming heard across the land. What am I?
Two round wheels and pedals too, I carry you the whole way through. What am I?
I fly at night and hoot so wise, with big round golden glowing eyes. What am I?
I buzz from flower to flower all day, and make sweet honey along the way. What am I?
Eight legs I have to spin my thread, catching flies within my web. What am I?
I hop from lily pad to log, and croak all night from in the bog. What am I?
I carry my house upon my back, and leave a slimy shiny track. What am I?
I sleep by day, hang upside down, and fly at night around the town. What am I?
In a tuxedo I always dress, on icy shores I love it best. What am I?
I hop on two strong springy feet, and keep my baby snug and neat. What am I?
I change my color as I please, to hide among the leaves and trees. What am I?
Eight long arms I use to swim, in ocean deep and dark and dim. What am I?
I fan my tail of shining blue, with eye-like spots that stare at you. What am I?
Across the desert sand I plod, a hump of fat is quite my mod. What am I?
I leap from waves with joyful grace, a friendly smile upon my face. What am I?
I blink my light on summer nights, a tiny lantern taking flight. What am I?
I curl into a spiky ball, when danger comes I fear no fall. What am I?
I tap the tree trunk all day long, rat-a-tat is my only song. What am I?
I'm named for a land animal, but swim upright and very small. What am I?
I build my dam of sticks and mud, to hold back the flowing flood. What am I?
On summer eves I chirp my tune, beneath the glowing silver moon. What am I?
The largest beast upon the land, with a trunk and tusks so grand. What am I?
My neck is long, I'm very tall, I reach the leaves above you all. What am I?
Slow and steady on I creep, my shell's the fortress that I keep. What am I?
The fastest runner on the plain, I catch my prey with speed insane. What am I?
White and graceful on the lake, a curving neck for beauty's sake. What am I?
I howl beneath the moon so bright, and hunt in packs throughout the night. What am I?
Red and clever, sly and quick, escaping traps is my best trick. What am I?
Sideways on the sand I walk, with pincer claws instead of talk. What am I?
I mimic every word you say, in feathers green and bright and gay. What am I?
I gather nuts and climb the tree, my bushy tail flicks after me. What am I?
Red with spots of blackest dot, a tiny beetle in the plot. What am I?
In eucalyptus trees I doze, munching leaves in sleepy pose. What am I?
Black and white and round and slow, on bamboo shoots I love to grow. What am I?
I float on my back in the stream, and crack a shell — a happy dream. What am I?
Beneath the ground I dig my hall, I rarely see the sun at all. What am I?
With mighty horns and thunderous snort, I charge the red cape as my sport. What am I?
I'm yellow and I have a peel, a monkey's favorite tasty meal. What am I?
Green outside and red within, with black seeds beneath my skin. What am I?
I start as tiny yellow seeds, then pop to white for movie needs. What am I?
Spiky crown and golden hide, sweet and juicy fruit inside. What am I?
From milk I'm made and often yellow, mice adore me, hungry fellow. What am I?
Golden, sticky, sweet, and thick, the bees all make me — take a lick. What am I?
Long and orange, crunchy too, rabbits love to nibble through. What am I?
Red and round, some call me fruit, in salads I am quite the beaut. What am I?
From flour and water I am kneaded, baked in ovens, warm and needed. What am I?
Yellow, sour, full of zest, in lemonade I taste the best. What am I?
Red and sweet with seeds outside, a summer treat none can hide. What am I?
Hard and brown and hairy shell, sweet white milk inside as well. What am I?
Small and round in bunches grown, to raisins I am sometimes thrown. What am I?
Orange and round in autumn air, carve my face for a Halloween scare. What am I?
Long and thin I twist and slide, in steaming soup I love to hide. What am I?
Small and red but full of fire, one bite raises your temper higher. What am I?
Red or green upon a tree, keep the doctor away from thee. What am I?
Round and bright, I share my name, with a color just the same. What am I?
Beneath the soil I grow in dirt, mashed or fried, I'll never hurt. What am I?
Cold and sweet on summer days, I melt beneath the sunny rays. What am I?
Flat and round upon your plate, with syrup poured, I taste so great. What am I?
Twisted, salty, baked with care, a knotted snack beyond compare. What am I?
Golden, juicy, tropical treat, no fruit I know is quite so sweet. What am I?
Round and leafy, layered tight, a green ball wrapped up nice and light. What am I?
In cloves I come with pungent smell, I flavor soups and stews so well. What am I?
Round with a hole right in my center, sugar-glazed for those who enter. What am I?
Square with pockets, crisp and light, I hold the syrup just right. What am I?
Small and red on slender stem, in pairs I hang, a shining gem. What am I?
Soft and fuzzy, sweet and round, the juiciest fruit that can be found. What am I?
Peel my layers and you may cry, I add my flavor to the fry. What am I?
After rain I arch the sky, seven colors way up high. What am I?
